type:
∀ (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [Ring R] [Ring S]
  (F : CategoryTheory.Functor (ModuleCat.{max u z} R) (ModuleCat.{w} S))
  [CategoryTheory.Functor.Additive F],
  let A := ModuleCat.of R (ULift.{z} R)
  let B := CategoryTheory.Functor.obj F A
  let rho : R → Quiver.Hom A A := fun r =>
    ModuleCat.ofHom
      (LinearEquiv.conjRingEquiv
        (LinearEquiv.symm (ULift.moduleEquiv : LinearEquiv (RingHom.id R) (ULift.{z} R) R))
        (LinearMap.mulRight R r))
  ∃ right : Module (MulOpposite R) ↥B,
    letI : Module (MulOpposite R) ↥B := right
    SMulCommClass (MulOpposite R) S ↥B ∧
      ∀ (r : R) (b : ↥B),
        SMul.smul (MulOpposite.op r) b =
          ModuleCat.Hom.hom (CategoryTheory.Functor.map F (rho r)) b
sourceReason:
The owner-specified cached TeX and PDF agree on Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Lemma 9.2 (env-9-2, p. 29). The rings are associative and unital, and the functor is additive between categories of unital left modules. The right R-action is a left Module over MulOpposite R commuting with the given left S-action. The left regular module is lifted to the source carrier universe by ULift. The conjugated left R-linear map sends a lifted x to the lift of x * r, and the theorem specifies the action by applying F to that map. https://getcurious.cc/downloads/abelian-categories-and-bimodules-lecture-notes.pdf#page=29
